title: The receiver toolchain hook test pins any installed Node other than the running one, and says so when it skips
body:
test/hook/receiver-toolchain.test.ts gates its two real-mise tests on `mise where node@24.22.1`: once the host prunes Node 24.22.1 (the workstation toolchain keeps one Node per tool), both tests stop running without a trace, and the hook's pin behaviour is no longer proven anywhere.
Files: test/hook/receiver-toolchain.test.ts
Outcome: the real-mise tests pick any installed Node whose full version differs from process.version (read from `mise ls --installed --json node`) and pin that, with the inner test asserting that exact version; when no such Node is installed they are reported as skipped with the reason (node:test `skip: '<reason>'`), never silently absent. No test names a fixed old Node version.
Proof: `node --test test/hook/receiver-toolchain.test.ts` prints pass for the real-mise tests on a host with a second Node installed, and a skip line with the reason when MISE data offers none.
